subject: health
unitTitle: Media, Technology, and Digital Influence on Health
essentialQuestion: Who profits when I believe a health claim, and how do I check before I share it?

prompts.prompt: Explain algorithmic feeds, engagement incentives, and health misinformation in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising.
Apply appearance filters, edited imagery, and body-image pressure in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving evaluating a health claim: source, evidence, plausibility, and incentive; correct it and explain why.
Connect privacy, data, and health information shared online with digital wellbeing: notification load, sleep, and attention. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Take apart three fictional but realistic health posts: identify the claim, the incentive, the evidence actually offered, and what a reliable source says instead. Write the correction you would actually post.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: Teardowns may be written, spoken, annotated on printouts, or completed on a supplied four-column template. No account creation, login, or live platform use is required.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
